To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) students' interdisciplinary learning is facilitated by the use of interdisciplinary tasks; (2) interdisciplinary tasks are effective when they require students to use knowledge from multiple disciplines and to integrate that knowledge to address a problem; and (3) interdisciplinary tasks that require students to integrate their knowledge across multiple domains are more effective than those that require students to apply knowledge from a single domain to a problem in a second domain.
interdisciplinary tasks are complex and require a variety of cognitive processes to complete.

interdisciplinary tasks can be analyzed using a three-part framework that includes: a) the disciplinary context of the task, b) the interdisciplinary nature of the task, and c) the interdisciplinary knowledge that is developed through the task.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to design curricular materials to help students learn about interdisciplinary phenomena.
understanding the nature of interdisciplinary tasks and how these tasks support student learning in introductory science.
understanding what it means to learn interdisciplinary science, and how interdisciplinary science can be taught.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the framework presented here can be used to analyze interdisciplinary learning tasks in order to identify the underlying learning objectives, and to design curricular materials that will support those learning objectives.

interdisciplinary science curricula can support interdisciplinary learning objectives when the curriculum is designed in a manner that explicitly addresses the following issues: 1) students must have the opportunity to engage with interdisciplinary problems, 2) the problems should be authentic, 3) students should be provided with the tools necessary to address the problems, 4) students must be able to communicate their findings in a manner that is understandable to their intended audience, and 5) students must have opportunities to reflect on the interdisciplinary nature of
the interdisciplinary tasks in this study were effective in helping students learn about interdisciplinary concepts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the framework provides a means to identify interdisciplinary tasks and to analyze the nature of the interdisciplinary learning that is expected of the learner.
we developed a framework for analyzing interdisciplinary tasks, and used that framework to identify and describe the components of interdisciplinary tasks that support interdisciplinary learning.

the framework provides a way to analyze the nature of interdisciplinary learning tasks and the cognitive demands they place on students, which is important for curriculum development and for understanding student learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
interdisciplinary tasks can be analyzed to reveal the underlying disciplinary concepts, practices, and perspectives.
interdisciplinary curricula should be designed to support students in making connections across disciplines.
the design of interdisciplinary tasks must take into account the nature of the disciplinary knowledge that will be used in the task.
